einzeiler: The final chapter of Julius Caesar covers his romance with Cleopatra, absolute rule, and…
kurzfassung: Julius Caesar emerges victorious from the civil war and begins a relationship with Queen Cleopatra of Egypt. After returning to Rome, he implements sweeping reforms, constructs monumental public works, and assumes the status of dictator for life. His consolidation of supreme power alienates traditionalists, culminating in his dramatic assassination by a group of senators on the Ides of March.
stichpunkte: Caesar meets Cleopatra in Alexandria, where she is smuggled into his quarters.
Following military victories in North Africa and Spain, Caesar returns to Rome to host massive celebrations.
He introduces the Julian calendar, reorganizing the year into 365 days with a leap year.
Caesar consolidates his authority by taking the title of dictator in perpetuity and building a new personal forum.
Conspirators led by Brutus and Cassius organize an assassination plot to protect republican traditions.
On the Ides of March in 44 BC, Caesar is murdered in the Senate at the Theatre of Pompey.
Mark Antony delivers a public speech that sparks riots and plunges Rome back into chaos.
Octavian eventually emerges as Caesar's heir, establishing the foundation for the Roman Empire.

clips.text: The famous queen arrives at the Roman leader's quarters hidden inside a laundry sack.
The speaker highlights massive statistics from triumphal parades, including thousands of tables of food and over a million claimed kills.

clips.hook: A golden throne and minted coins
clips.text: The ruler begins displaying overt signs of monarchy by sitting on a golden throne and placing his own face on currency.

clips.hook: A prophetic wish for a sudden end
clips.text: When asked about a preferred way to die during a dinner party, the doomed leader answers that he desires a swift and sudden exit.
Contrary to popular theatrical adaptations, the dying dictator utters his last phrase in Greek rather than Latin.

beschreibung:
Caesar departs Egypt with his lover, Cleopatra, secure on the throne. After crushing Pompey’s allies, he returns to Rome. His rule proves popular with the masses. But senators grow concerned by his increasing megalomania. With the Ides of March approaching, conspirators hatch an historic assassination plot…
